analysis:
Examined the head text of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift (lines 552-1706) and the StartupPreload patch. Changed behavior: (1) addonHoldLoadRefusal(for:) fences model loads at the load-gate entry (patch hunk near line 396), after the weight-hash capture (head line 577), and through modelLoadInterruption (lines 711 and 945, helper at 1046-1049). (2) persistLoadedModelSet now skips writes while addonHoldActive (StartupPreload.swift line 106), so a temporary hold-induced unload does not overwrite the persisted serving set.

Threat relevance: T-059 / TB-012 / A-018, a local process holding the provider out of routing. The new refusals narrow the window in which weights are loaded beside running VMs. Interruption paths on the error branches call newcomer.releaseAfterExternalResources, clearCache, and unwindHoldingResliceGate / releaseResliceGate before throwing. The reslice gate, pending-load lease, and loading waiters are released in the catch block (lines 988-1039), so there is no visible gate leak or deadlock. The 945-949 path unwinds the built slot and releases the gate before throwing, and the installed slot is only published after the interruption check. The weight-hash TOCTOU verification (artifactIdentityRequired, bracketing post-load hash, finalizeReusableSSDLoad) is unchanged. The cache-eligibility flow tied to T-041 is unchanged, and no new at-rest artifacts are introduced.

Remaining unverified: the definitions of addonHoldLoadRefusal and addonHoldActive, and where addonHoldActive is cleared. They are outside the supplied evidence. If a hold is never cleared, persistence stays suppressed, so the persisted set could go stale. This is an availability or state-staleness concern for the integration pass and is not demonstrable here. Also unverified: whether the retirement paths for native MiMo and Nemotron Super (not shown) call persistLoadedModelSet consistently. No concrete security regression is identified in the supplied lines.
